metadata.notes: Web-checked precise local anniversaries, separated event start/crest/landfall timelines, and preserved existing alternatives. Historical source dependencies and media rights still unresolved.

reviews.title_before: Dense Fog — C W BOX ELDER/C W XE TOOLE/X W SALT LAKE/X NW UTAH, Utah
reviews.title_after: Category 5 Cyclone Yasi strikes Queensland's tropical coast overnight
reviews.core_fact: Severe Tropical Cyclone Yasi made landfall near Mission Beach, Queensland, shortly after midnight in the early morning of February 3, 2011 (Queensland local time).
reviews.source_dependence: Bureau of Meteorology post-analysis documents landfall time and category; ABC contemporary Australian reporting independently confirms the place/date but follows the bureau for storm classification.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use Queensland AEST, not AEDT; local February 3 versus UTC February 2 can confuse the anniversary. Australian cyclone Category 5 is NOT the U.S. SSHWS Category 5; gust estimates and post-analysis central pressures need source-specific attribution.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Queensland coastline, landfall timing and observed pressure/wind timeline

reviews.title_before: Winter Storm — YAVAPAI COUNTY VALLEYS AND BASINS, Arizona
reviews.title_after: A warm atmospheric river unleashes flooding around California's Kern River
reviews.location_after: Kernville and Southern Sierra Nevada, California
reviews.core_fact: A strong atmospheric river produced heavy rain and flash flooding around Kernville and the Kern River on March 10, 2023, following heavy winter mountain snowfall.
reviews.source_dependence: The original NWS WPC March10 storm summary and contemporary Los Angeles Times flood/evacuation reporting independently establish California event/date; news coverage cites some NWS observations.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Differentiate March 9 atmospheric-river arrival, March 10 major flooding and subsequent March 11–14 impacts. Warm rain and snowmelt contributed in varying watersheds; not every reported high water mark originated on March 10. Avoid overclaiming exact flow or return periods.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original moisture-flux and rain-on-snow schematic with Kern River basin and verified March10 flood times

reviews.title_after: Cyclone Kenneth slams northern Mozambique only weeks after Idai
reviews.core_fact: Tropical Cyclone Kenneth made landfall in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado Province on the evening of April 25, 2019, after another damaging cyclone, Idai, had struck Mozambique weeks earlier.
reviews.source_dependence: WMO regional weather chronology, UNDP local response reporting and NASA Terra satellite imagery separately corroborate April25 landfall, though UN agencies often share operational best-track data.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Kenneth and Idai were separate cyclones; landfall Mozambique local time April25 is central. WMO says unusual for Cabo Delgado in satellite era, not 'first cyclone ever'. Avoid translating SW Indian Ocean intensity categories directly into Saffir–Simpson categories or quoting early casualty totals.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Mozambique map showing Kenneth landfall and Idai's distinct earlier track, with UTC/local times

reviews.title_after: Dry thunderstorms and shifting winds threaten Colorado's Black Forest fire
reviews.location_after: Black Forest, El Paso County, Colorado
reviews.core_fact: Colorado's Black Forest wildfire, which began June 11, 2013, continued spreading and prompting evacuations on June 13 amid dangerous dry and gusty fire-weather conditions.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Pueblo weather retrospective explains meteorological context; NASA June13 image/report documents date and expanding fire, while contemporary Colorado Public Radio time-stamped updates provide separate evacuation context.
reviews.unverified_cautions: June 13 was an expansion and evacuation day, NOT the June 11 ignition date. Strong/erratic winds and dry lightning forecasts are not proof that lightning ignited this specific wildfire; sources describe different fire-size estimates at different report times. State 'active on June13' rather than started.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Black Forest fire growth map on June13 with wind shifts, relative humidity and evacuation areas

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — GREATER  PORTLAND METRO AREA, Oregon
reviews.title_after: The Amite River crests at record flood stage in Denham Springs
reviews.location_after: Amite River at Denham Springs, Livingston Parish, Louisiana
reviews.core_fact: The Amite River at Denham Springs rose during the August 2016 Louisiana flood and reached a record crest early on Sunday, August 14, following days of extraordinary rainfall.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS streamgage hydrograph supplies independent hydrological timing; NASA satellite/aerial coverage documents the flood extent on August14, but does not independently measure the same river crest.
reviews.unverified_cautions: August14 is the Denham Springs gauge's crest, not the maximum rainfall for every basin. Amite, Comite and Tickfaw peak times differ. Distinguish gage height from above-ground inundation depth, and observed stage from preliminary/final data; avoid using unlicensed flood photographs.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original USGS Denham Springs hydrograph and basin-scale upstream rainfall-to-crest timeline

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Ivan's outer rainbands spawn destructive tornadoes near Blountstown
reviews.core_fact: On September 15, 2004, tornadoes embedded in Hurricane Ivan's outer rainbands struck parts of the Florida Panhandle, including a damaging F2 near Blountstown.
reviews.source_dependence: The original NCEI county event and NWS Tallahassee operational retrospective describe the same tornado surveys, so second publisher is corroborating the date/location, not creating an independent intensity measurement.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Ivan's hurricane center did not make U.S. landfall until early September 16; the tornadoes occurred on September15. Preserve historical F2 rather than EF2. Do not attach all Ivan tornado losses or 130 tornado warnings to this one surveyed Blountstown track.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Ivan outer-band radar storm-relative hodograph and surveyed Florida tornado path inset

reviews.title_after: An October lake-effect snowstorm buries Buffalo while trees still have leaves
reviews.location_after: Buffalo and eastern Lake Erie shore, New York
reviews.core_fact: A rare early-season lake-effect storm produced damaging heavy wet snow around Buffalo on October 12–13, 2006; the event ended on October 13 with 22.6 inches recorded at Buffalo's airport.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS event archive and regional reporting substantiate Oct13 and widespread damage; peer-reviewed AMS lightning study analyzes unusual convection but generally reuses NWS snowfall totals.
reviews.unverified_cautions: 22.6 inches is a two-day storm total, NOT 22.6 inches recorded solely on October13. Airport totals differ from downtown amounts; leaves remaining on trees and high water content increased tree failures. Do not generalize snowfall totals outside narrow lake-effect band.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Lake Erie fetch, vertical thermal profile and dated snowfall swath showing leaf-laden tree impacts

reviews.title_after: An F3 tornado strikes Henry County, Tennessee, late at night
reviews.core_fact: A damaging F3 tornado struck Henry County near Paris, Tennessee, around 11:30 p.m. CST on November 26, 2001, two days after a separate F2 tornado near Murray, Kentucky.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI historical segment and NWS Paducah event retrospective document the same NWS survey; these are corroborating archival sources rather than independent modern Doppler/engineering validation.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The secondary NWS page is titled 'November24 Tornado' because that was a separate KY F2 and the text includes the NOV26 TN F3. Do not swap the two tracks, dates, injuries or fatality figures. Historical F3, not EF3.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original two-date western Kentucky / Tennessee comparison map, separate Nov24 and Nov26 surveyed tracks

reviews.title_after: Unusually early deep snow paralyzes parts of Britain in December 2010
reviews.location_after: United Kingdom, including Scotland and northern England
reviews.core_fact: An exceptional early-winter snow and cold outbreak affected parts of the United Kingdom on December 2, 2010, when the Forth Road Bridge was closed for hours.
reviews.source_dependence: Met Office snowfall case study documents December2 snow and bridge disruption; University of Reading's independent contemporaneous weather diary documents station/weather observations, but uses some official synoptic information.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The episode began in late November and continued across December; distinguish the 0900 GMT Dec2 snow-depth observing time and bridge closure from storm-total snowfall. Forth Road Bridge is not Forth rail bridge; don't confuse this episode with another December 2010 cold spell before Christmas.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 0900 GMT December2 UK snow-cover and pressure map with traffic impacts and time labels

alternate_reviews.title: A remarkable Kentucky snowstorm begins, with deep snow following through February 6
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: Original county Storm Data record and NWS Louisville climatology share the same climate observations; NWS Nashville documents broader regional progression separately.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: The extraordinary February 3–6, 1998 snowstorm began the evening of February 3, with heavy snow across Louisville and northern Kentucky.
alternate_reviews.caution: February3 is beginning, not day of all-time snow depth; Louisville largest single-day amount was Feb4, while storm totals accumulated Feb3–6. NWS current airport totals and older NCEI station totals need reconciliation.

alternate_reviews.title: Strong winds rekindle prescribed-burn embers into Colorado's Lower North Fork wildfire
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NCEI local wildfire record and formal incident lessons-learned report corroborate start and weather; ignition mechanism derives from investigation, not independent station wind determination.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: On March 26, 2012, strong winds lofted hot embers from a previously completed prescribed burn south of Conifer, causing the Lower North Fork wildfire.
alternate_reviews.caution: March22 prescribed-fire ignition, March26 escaped wildfire and later fire perimeter/fatality reporting are different dates. Weather was an escape/spread factor, not the original March22 ignition; distinguish red flag forecast from realized wind observations.

alternate_reviews.title: Training storms cause a fatal flash flood near Elk City Lake, Kansas
alternate_reviews.location: Elk City Lake and Racket Creek, Montgomery County, Kansas
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: The NCEI county-local record and NWS Wichita storm review share gauge/radar estimates and emergency-management reports; contemporaneous local reporting supplies another narrative source.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: Intense thunderstorms produced deadly flash flooding near Elk City Lake in southeast Kansas on August 14, 2018.
alternate_reviews.caution: This alternate duplicates the flood hazard of Aug14 Louisiana's 2016 primary, though it's a different meteorological event and region. Racket Creek flash flood is not uniform Elk City Lake reservoir stage; 24-hour rainfall estimates versus totals should not be conflated.

alternate_reviews.title: Santa Ana winds fan the newly ignited Thomas Fire across Ventura County
alternate_reviews.location: Santa Paula and Ventura County, California
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NCEI county weather record and Ventura County Fire Department cause investigation support original ignition date and wind influence; investigators provide primary fire-origin evidence.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: The Thomas Fire began near Santa Paula during powerful Santa Ana winds on the evening of December 4, 2017, before spreading toward Ventura.
alternate_reviews.caution: Power-line contact during high winds is a documented ignition mechanism, not spontaneous ignition from 'hot wind'. December4 start versus December5 major area growth and subsequent final burned acreage must be distinguished; no use of unlicensed fire photos.

editorial_deferrals: Dec04 Thomas Fire is the ORIGINAL FIRST ALTERNATE and has been corroborated as an alternate; it was not promoted to primary because that would duplicate the same event under two IDs.
Apr17 Houston Tax Day Flood on Apr17/18 is well documented but deferred to avoid two adjacent flood-category primaries (Apr18 already Chicago training storms).
Oct06 2016 Matthew struck Bahamas but Oct07 already has a tropical primary (Hurricane Nate); avoid consecutive tropical days until alternatives are improved.
Sep03 2019 Dorian stalled over Grand Bahama but Sep04 is another unverified hurricane primary; avoid another back-to-back tropical sequence.
June13 Black Forest fire was already burning after June11 ignition; feature June13 dangerous winds and expansion, NEVER imply ignition that date.
August14 Elk City Lake Kansas alternate shares flood category but represents independent two-years-later rain/flash-flood event.
